title: Combine filters
description: Combine ordinary and related-record filters, control how groups match, and require distinct related performers when one match is not enough.

blocks.text: Select a group's operator when the conditions should relate differently. The operator applies only to the direct conditions and subgroups inside that group.

items: All requires every direct condition or group to match.
Any requires at least one direct condition or group to match.
Just One requires exactly one direct condition or group to match.
None requires every direct condition or group not to match.

blocks.text: Each Related Performers condition can itself require several facts about the same performer. Its relationship mode controls whether at least one performer, every performer, or no performer must match those nested facts. The surrounding group then controls how the separate relationship conditions work together.
Age (now) uses the performer's current age. Use Age (then) when the age at the video's date is what matters.
Select a condition to edit it, or select a group operator to change its direct children. A condition's menu can move or remove it.

items: Open the group menu and choose Create subgroup.
Select the sibling conditions that belong together.
Choose All, Any, Just One, or None for the new group.

blocks.text: A subgroup lets only part of the search use a different rule. You can dissolve it later without losing its conditions. Choose Cancel grouping to leave the search unchanged. A None subgroup can contain one or more selections; the other subgroup types need at least two.

For keyboard control, Tab moves between control groups, arrow keys move within controls that use roving focus, and Enter or Space activates the focused control. Escape closes the current picker or menu, cancels a keyboard move, or returns to the preceding filter view.

Apply the filter and check that the result represents the question you meant to ask. If it is a view you will revisit, save it only after that check so the named filter preserves the finished expression.
Use these practical combinations as starting points, then replace the example values with the ones that matter in your library.

items.title: Include archive URLs but exclude private entries
items.description: Combine two URL conditions in one All group.

blocks.text: The permanent demo library includes public and private archive URLs on its records, so you can reproduce this example after any demo reset.

items: Open Videos, choose Filters, and select URL.
Set the first condition to Includes and enter archive.example.
Choose Add another URL, set it to Excludes, and enter /private/.
Open Combine Filters and leave the two URL conditions in an All group.
Choose Apply. The result contains archive URLs except those in the private path.

blocks.alt: All group with URL Includes archive.example and URL Excludes private path conditions
blocks.caption: All requires both URL statements to be true for the same video.

blocks.text: Excludes also matches a record with no URL containing that text. Pairing it with Includes archive.example ensures the result has an archive URL first, then removes the private subset.

items.title: Require different performers in overlapping age ranges
items.description: Use distinct match assignment when separate related records must satisfy separate conditions.

items: In Videos, add Related Performers and choose Age (now).
Choose + in the bottom-left corner to add another performer condition, set its Age (now) to Between 30 and 49, then choose Apply to add the condition.
Open Combine Filters and leave both conditions in an All group.
Set both relationship conditions to At least one matching performer, then choose Use a different performer for each under Match assignment.
Choose Apply to use the completed filter.

blocks.text: May reuse a performer allows one performer aged 30 through 40 to satisfy both conditions. Use a different performer for each instead requires one related performer for each range; Cove assigns the matches rather than merely counting performers on the video.

blocks.alt: Related Performers group with two overlapping age ranges and Use a different performer for each selected
blocks.caption: Distinct assignment is useful when several related records must play different roles in one result.

blocks.text: If the ranges overlap, switching between reuse and distinct assignment is an easy way to confirm that the relationship changes the result set.
